key_insight: EC-Bench introduces a focused benchmark for enumeration and counting in ultra-long videos, shifting evaluation from single final counts to temporally grounded instance-level consistency across minutes-to-hours recordings. It reveals that counting in long, sparse, diverse video streams requires new annotation, evaluation and baseline protocols to measure when and what is being counted.
problem_solved: Current video counting benchmarks use short clips and only final numeric answers, which fail to capture long-range temporal reasoning, sparse event occurrence, and whether models consistently identify relevant instances over ultra-long recordings.
method: Curate and annotate a collection of ultra-long videos with temporally localized instance-level counting labels and clear counting definitions for diverse real-world scenes.
Design evaluation protocols and metrics that measure both final count accuracy and temporal consistency/localization (e.g., per-interval counts, detection consistency, error accumulation over time).
Provide baseline model implementations and benchmarking recipes to evaluate performance, failure modes, and scalability on long-duration inputs.
impact: EC-Bench enables researchers and practitioners to diagnose and improve long-range temporal reasoning and robustness for counting tasks, guiding development of models and training strategies that operate reliably on minutes- to hours-long video streams.
visual_elements: Timeline visualization showing ground-truth vs. predicted counts across the full video duration (per-interval line chart).
Raster/heatmap of event density over time with annotated instance markers to show sparsity and clustering.
Bar chart comparing final-count accuracy, temporal-consistency score, and localization error across baseline models.
Sample frame strip with instance-level annotations and a legend explaining counting rules (what counts vs. what doesn’t).
paper_title: EC-Bench: Enumeration and Counting Benchmark for Ultra-Long Videos
paper_authors: Fumihiko Tsuchiya, Taiki Miyanishi, Mahiro Ukai, Nakamasa Inoue, Shuhei Kurita
